conventions: confirmed=true means the figure was read on the fetched page itself; false means it came only from a search-engine summary or a page that could not be fetched (403/404/timeout). Currency as published.

rule.text: One identification document issued by a Canadian federal, provincial or territorial government that includes photo, full name and date of birth; otherwise two government-issued documents showing name, one with full name and date of birth. Provincial/territorial documents listed include birth certificate, driver's licence, health card and identification card. Hunting, boating and fishing licenses are not accepted; ID must not be expired; name must match the boarding pass.
rule.note: The requirement stems from Transport Canada's Passenger Protect / Identity Screening Regulations; the airline checks ID at check-in and the gate. The CATSA page URL tried returned 404.

ontario_photo_card_fee.text: $35 fee, for a new card and for a renewal

bcid_fee.other: Reported free for seniors 65+ and free when exchanging a driver's license for a BCID.
bcid_fee.note: ICBC's BCID page says 'pay the fee' without the amount, and its Fees page table did not render (loaded by script). $35 new / $15 renewal comes from search summaries of ICBC and third-party pages only.

ine_accepted_domestic.text: ASA (Aeropuertos y Servicios Auxiliares) lists these official photo IDs for domestic flights: passport, professional license (cédula profesional), military service booklet (cartilla militar), driver's license and the INE/IFE voter credential. It must be current and legible.
ine_accepted_domestic.note: Secondary press citing ASA; an ASA/AFAC primary page was not fetched.

ine_cost.text: "Tramitar tu Credencial para Votar (también conocida como INE) es completamente gratuito."

united_kingdom.note: UK law does not set an ID rule for domestic flights; each airline sets its own. Children under 16 flying with an adult generally need no ID.

british_airways.text: Since 2023-09-01 BA requires passengers 16+ on UK domestic flights to show photo ID such as a passport, a driving license or a valid EU national identity card (other sources add armed forces ID and police warrant card).
british_airways.note: ba.com's travel-documents page returned a high-demand holding page; not read on BA's own site.

easyjet.text: Photo ID required on all UK domestic flights: valid passport, valid photographic EU or Swiss national ID card, valid photographic driving license (provisional or full), armed forces ID card, police warrant card/badge.
easyjet.note: easyJet's page returned 403; the list is from search summaries, including an easyJet reply on X (https://x.com/easyJet/status/2054509262471348667) stating a provisional or full photo driving license is accepted.

passport_card_fee.text: €35 online; valid 5 years or until the passport book expires, whichever comes first; only issued to holders of a valid Irish passport book. Bundle with an adult 10-year passport is €100 (a €10 saving). €15 postal fee if living outside Ireland.
passport_card_fee.note: The DFA and Citizens Information pages returned 403; €35, the €100 bundle and the €15 postal fee match their search snippets.

aer_lingus.text: From 2026-02-25 all customers, including Irish and British nationals, on Aer Lingus and Aer Lingus Regional between Ireland and the UK need a valid passport or an Irish passport card; driving licenses and other photo ID are no longer accepted. Exempt: domestic Aer Lingus Regional (Emerald Airlines) services, e.g. Belfast–UK and Dublin–Donegal. The passport card is also valid throughout the EU/EEA and Switzerland.

ryanair.text: Ryanair: "the airline does in fact accept Irish Passport Cards as a valid travel document for travel to/from all EU member states, Norway, Switzerland and the UK." Ryanair accepts only passports and national ID cards (not driving licenses) and has long required a passport on Ireland–UK flights.
ryanair.note: Ryanair's help center returned 403, so the current wording was not read there.

hotel_fees.summary: No chain publishes one early check-in or late check-out fee; each hotel sets its own. The published figures below are property-specific.

incidental_holds.text: To cover incidentals, we'll hold $150/day on your credit card.
To cover incidentals, we'll hold $150/day on your credit card.
pre-authorisation ... to cover room and incidental costs (£200 per night, to a maximum of three nights)

incidental_holds.per: night, on top of room and tax
incidental_holds.text: Room rate plus about $50 per night is typical; luxury and resort properties can exceed $100.
$50–$100 a night at standard brands; $150+ at Waldorf Astoria/Conrad; some budget brands a flat $50 per stay.

early_check_in.note: marriott.com returned 403; figure from the search summary only.

late_check_out.per: hour until 2 PM; a full night after 2 PM
late_check_out.note: Page returned 403; from the search summary.

late_check_out.text: Late check-out fees apply after 12pm (amount not published). Check-in 4 PM, check-out 12 PM.
Early check-in and late check-out subject to availability; 'a fee may apply' (amount not published). Check-in 3 PM, check-out 12 PM.
Platinum, Titanium and Ambassador Elite get guaranteed 4 PM late checkout at most properties (not resort/convention hotels); Gold gets 2 PM subject to availability.

hotel_fees.not_found: No published early check-in or late check-out fee from a London or Toronto chain hotel was read on the page itself; no Hilton official incidental-hold figure was found.

source.note: Read by extracting the PDF's text myself.

bc_ferries.general: One-way fares in CAD, taxes included. A 5% fuel surcharge is added at payment to net fares (not stowage). Vehicle fare excludes driver and passengers.

reservation_fee.text: Customers looking to book ahead, but not prepay, can purchase a separate reservation fee costing $20, and pay the At-Terminal tariff on departure.

tsawwassen_swartz_bay_route_1.other: Motorcycle $44.50; extra length over 20 ft $8.00/ft; seniors free Monday–Thursday except statutory holidays.

horseshoe_bay_to_departure_bay_route_2.reservation_fee: None separately; vehicles must book and pay in advance (Prepaid, which includes a booking, or Saver). This applies since 2025-10-15, in the Horseshoe Bay → Departure Bay direction only.
horseshoe_bay_to_departure_bay_route_2.extra: Nanaimo Port Authority fee $0.50 per adult, $0.30 per child 5–11.

stena_line_dublin_holyhead.sailings: 8 times daily (as published on the route page)

foot_passenger_fare.note: Not published on Stena's route pages. Aggregators give ranges (about €26–€72, dynamically priced); not confirmed on a primary page.

sample_timetable.text: Stena Line departs Dublin Port Terminal 2 at 08:15, arrives Holyhead 11:50; London→Dublin direction sails Holyhead 15:15, arrives Dublin 18:30.
sample_timetable.note: Only one deepwater berth has operated at Holyhead since storm damage in late 2024, still in 2026, per the same page.

avanti_holyhead_london_euston.text: Direct Avanti West Coast train departs Holyhead 12:48, arrives London Euston 16:37 (Monday–Friday), about 3 h 49 min. Outbound London Euston 09:00 → Holyhead 12:50 (3 h 40 min). Total central Dublin → Euston is roughly 8–9 hours.

sailrail_through_ticket.text: Adult single €58.00; double for return; same-day purchase supplement €6 single; children 5–15 half fare, 0–4 free; no services 25–26 December; book by phone +353 1 871 4788. Other stations: Bangor/Llandudno/Rhyl €51, Chester/Manchester/Liverpool €52, Birmingham/Leeds/Coventry €53, Bristol/Milton Keynes/Watford €55.
Advance Rail & Sail fares from £46.10 each way; children half price; no First Class; no railcard discounts; ferry reservation compulsory. The page also says these tickets 'are not available yet'.

dublin_london_rail_and_sail.id_note: Avanti's page says that as of September 28 a valid passport or Irish passport card is required to board ferries to Dublin; driving licenses and national ID cards are no longer accepted (year not stated on the page; read 2026-09-30).
